package_info.package_manager: Linux distribution package managers (e.g., apt, yum, pacman)
package_info.package_versions: 5.6.0, 5.6.1 (as referenced in the XZ supply chain attack; these are the known compromised versions)
package_info.why_malicious: The XZ package was compromised with malicious code that specifically targeted the SSH process (sshd), enabling attackers to bypass SSH authentication and gain unauthorized remote access to Linux servers. This constitutes a severe supply chain attack, as the malicious code was covertly inserted into a widely used open source compression library, impacting the security of any system that installed the affected versions and undermining the trust in the software supply chain.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when the OpenSSH server (sshd) is started and dynamically links against the compromised XZ library
execution_context.file_location: liblzma/configure.ac and liblzma/src/liblzma/api/lzma.h (malicious build scripts and code were inserted in these and related files; exact file may vary by distribution, but these are referenced in public advisories)
required_permissions: filesystem (to be loaded as a shared library)
process control (to hook/intercept SSH authentication routines)
network (to potentially enable remote access or exfiltration)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: /* Malicious code was inserted into the XZ library's build system and source files, resulting in a backdoor that hooks into the SSH authentication process. The code is obfuscated and split across multiple files, but its core function is to intercept authentication checks in sshd and allow unauthorized access. (Exact code is not provided in the report, but public advisories reference inserted logic in configure.ac and lzma.h.) */
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when sshd loads the compromised XZ library, the malicious code hooks into the SSH authentication routines, intercepts and manipulates authentication logic, and enables unauthorized remote access for the attacker, resulting in a full server compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code introduces hidden hooks into the SSH authentication process, a critical security boundary, allowing attackers to bypass normal authentication and gain remote access. This behavior is highly anomalous for a compression library and directly undermines system security.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: The XZ library is expected to provide only compression and decompression functionality. It should never interact with authentication mechanisms, modify process memory of sshd, or introduce hooks into security-critical routines.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate scenario where a compression library such as XZ would need to interact with or modify SSH authentication logic. Any such behavior is inherently suspicious and outside the scope of normal library operations.
key_indicators: Presence of obfuscated or hidden code in XZ source or build scripts
XZ library being loaded into the sshd process and modifying authentication routines
Unexpected changes to configure.ac, lzma.h, or related files introducing process hooks
Behavior enabling SSH authentication bypass or remote access not present in official XZ releases

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is covertly inserted into the XZ open source library's source and build scripts, and released as part of official updates (versions 5.6.0 and 5.6.1).
attack_chain.leads_to: Distribution of the compromised package to downstream users and Linux distributions

attack_chain.action: Organizations and users update or install the affected XZ package via their Linux distribution's package manager, integrating the compromised library into their systems.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is present and active on production systems

attack_chain.action: When the OpenSSH server (sshd) is started, it dynamically links against the compromised XZ library, triggering the malicious code to execute and intercept SSH authentication routines.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can bypass SSH authentication and gain unauthorized remote access

attack_chain.action: Attacker leverages unauthorized SSH access to compromise the server, potentially escalating privileges and moving laterally within the network.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full system compromise and potential lateral movement across the environment

behavioral_signatures: Compression libraries (such as XZ) being loaded into the sshd process and modifying authentication logic
Unexpected process hooking or code execution within sshd originating from liblzma or XZ-related shared libraries
Anomalous runtime behavior when SSH is invoked, such as new code paths, memory modifications, or authentication bypass events
file_indicators: /usr/lib/liblzma.so.5.6.0 or /usr/lib/liblzma.so.5.6.1 with unexpected changes or additional code
XZ package versions 5.6.0 or 5.6.1 installed (as per dpkg, rpm, or pacman queries)
Presence of obfuscated or suspicious code in configure.ac, lzma.h, or related build/source files
network_indicators: Unusual outbound connections initiated by sshd or XZ-related processes (if exfiltration is present)
Unexpected remote SSH access patterns or authentication bypass events following XZ package updates
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for installation or updates of XZ package versions 5.6.0 and 5.6.1. Perform file integrity checks on liblzma.so and related files, comparing against known-good hashes. Use behavioral monitoring to detect compression libraries being loaded into sshd and any process hooking or authentication bypass activity. Investigate any anomalous SSH authentication events, especially following recent XZ updates. Cross-reference installed package versions with security advisories on the XZ supply chain attack. Review build scripts and source files for obfuscated or unauthorized code changes.
